title: Maximize Palindrome Length From Subsequences
summary: Given two strings, select non-empty subsequences from each, concatenate them, and determine the maximum possible length of a palindrome.
statement: Given two strings, select non-empty subsequences from each, concatenate them, and determine the maximum possible length of a palindrome. If no palindrome can be formed, return 0. A subsequence is formed by deleting some characters from a string without altering the order of the remaining characters. A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards.
constraints: Choose a nonempty subsequence from each word and concatenate them in word order.
Return the maximum possible palindrome length, or zero if none can use characters from both words.
hints: A valid answer must contain a matching outer pair with its left character in word1 and right character in word2.
Compute longest-palindromic-subsequence DP on the concatenated text.
Whenever a matching transition crosses the word boundary, use its DP length to update the answer.
Every valid cross-word palindrome has such an outer cross-boundary matching pair, and the interval DP optimizes its interior.
editorial: Every valid cross-word palindrome has such an outer cross-boundary matching pair, and the interval DP optimizes its interior.

tests.explanation: Choosing ac from word1 and bca from word2 forms acbca of length five.
Choosing a from each word gives palindrome aa of length two.
